The collapse of marathon climate talks in Turkey has renewed questions about reform of their consensus requirement, and galvanised calls for legal action and ambitious side agreements between like-minded countries.
The "conference of the parties" talks, better known as COP31, ended without agreement and two days over schedule on Sunday, as countries deadlocked on fossil fuels, finance, science and carbon-removing technologies.

items.title: Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
items.content:
Trump claims he predicted drops in oil prices, stock market and hits from Iran after Democratic win in midterm elections
US president Donald Trump claimed that he predicted a stock market decline as well as harsher attacks from Iran after the Democratic victory in the recent midterm elections.
"As everyone remembers, I predicted two things concerning the November 3rd Midterm Elections. One, that if the Democrats win, the Stock Markets would go down, substantially, which they have, and two, that the Islamic Republic of Iran... will grow more aggressive in their attacks, which has also occurred," he wrote in a post on his platform Truth Social.
Trump added that Iran "launched more drones and missiles in the last week than at any time for over a year," but claimed that the attacks have "all been knocked down, and done no damage".
"Iranian leaders consider the Democrats weak, ineffective, and Country destroying, but I won’t let that happen! Both the Dems and Iran fought like hell to keep the Oil price up as long as possible and, since the Election, the Oil price has dropped by a record level," the American president further claimed.
Trump went onto describe the elections as "very strange".
In another post, he questioned the drop in oil prices, saying: "Isn’t it interesting that Oil prices have dropped precipitously after the Midterm Elections? I said that was going to happen. The whole thing is a Giant Hoax!"

items.title: Fewer than half in UK will pay TV licence fee within a decade, report warns
items.content:
Analysis for thinktank points to cycle of falling income leading to lower spending on content in ‘spiral of decline’
Fewer than half of households in Britain will pay the BBC’s licence within a decade, according to analysis that warns that the broadcaster’s funding is locked in a
“spiral of decline”
.
With senior BBC figures
concerned about the accelerating fall
in licence fee sales, the independent projections also warn that the proportion of households paying the levy will further decline to less than a third by 2037-38 should the government persist with the corporation’s current funding model.

items.title: Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland’, experts find
items.content:
Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’
Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.
Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.

items.title: Saudi Arabia's influence loomed large over failed COP31 deal
items.content:
By Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - As the COP31 climate conference drifted into what proved to be record overtime, a negotiator from a small island state complained that a promised meeting with the talks' Turkish and Australian presidents had been cancelled yet again.
Saudi officials, meanwhile, had regular access, allowing them disproportionate influence at the Antalya conference, according to negotiators from Europe, small island states, Latin America, Asia and Africa.

items.content:

Video of the incident on Saturday – filmed by fellow passengers – quickly went viral on social media, sparking condemnation from lawmakers, including Washington Democratic governor Bob Ferguson and Seattle mayor Katie Wilson.

items.title: South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran
items.content:
South Korea says deployment to Middle East not indirect military participation in war on Iran
South Korean Defence Minister Kang Shin-chul said that a motion to extend the deployment of the Cheonghae anti-piracy unit in the Gulf of Aden did not amount to involvement in the US-Israeli war on Iran.
The minister told lawmakers that the deployment was not indirect military participation in the conflict, but instead cited a rise in piracy alongside efforts to protect South Korean ships and citizens using the maritime route.

items.title: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
items.content:
Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
Turkey's foreign minister has warned that Israel could launch a military operation in Syria, accusing it of backing a faction within the country's Druze community in an attempt to provoke the Syrian army and create a pretext for intervention.
Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials.
"There is a scenario in which the Israeli army uses this as a pretext to launch an operation against Syria," Fidan said.
The Turkish foreign minister also alleged that Israel was supporting one of three major factions within Syria's Druze community, supplying it with weapons and ammunition by helicopter on a weekly basis.
Read more:
Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?

items.title: Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
items.content:
Watch: Palestinians describe fear after Israeli settlers attack West Bank villages
Palestinian residents in the occupied West Bank have described how Israeli settlers set fire to vehicles and sprayed racist graffiti on homes during overnight attacks on several villages.
Footage from Deir Abu Mashal and Kafr Malik on Sunday shows burnt-out cars and graffiti reading "Death to Arabs" and "Revenge" painted on walls. Residents said settlers attacked their villages while families were asleep, leaving multiple vehicles destroyed.
"We were sleeping and not expecting that herds of settlers will attack our homes while people are sleeping, we never expected this," said Muneer Alkhatib, a resident of Deir Abu Mashal.
Another resident, Montaser Almalki, said the attackers came from a nearby settler outpost and warned that his family could have been caught in a fire had they not woken up.
The attacks took place across several locations in the occupied West Bank. They were condemned by Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot, who described them as "Jewish terrorism" and blamed far-right ministers Itamar Ben Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich for encouraging the violence.

items.title: Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon
items.content:
Israel carries out more demolitions in southern Lebanon
Israeli
forces detonated explosives to destroy structures on the outskirts of Qantara in southern
Lebanon
, Lebanon's National News Agency (NNA) reported.
Earlier on Sunday, Israeli forces set off a massive explosion in Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, followed by another in Kfar Tibnit, according to NNA.
The blasts could be heard across much of southern Lebanon.
Residents of Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Zawtar held two separate protests against the Lebanese government's "silence" over Israel's occupation of areas up to the Litani River, which began in March, according to NNA.
Parliament Speaker Nabih Berri said he would not accept congratulations on Lebanon's Independence Day, which falls on 22 November, in solidarity with residents of the occupied southern border villages.
In a statement, Berri described this year's independence as "incomplete and unfulfilled".
He said it would be complete only once Lebanese territory was liberated and official and popular positions were united again.

items.title: Eisenkot condemns 'Jewish terrorism' near Ramallah as US congressman calls for accountability
items.content:
Eisenkot condemns 'Jewish terrorism' near Ramallah as US congressman calls for accountability
Israeli politician Gadi Eisenkot has condemned a series of arson attacks by settlers in the occupied West Bank as "Jewish terrorism", accusing far-right ministers Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben Gvir of fuelling violence against Palestinians.
Overnight into Sunday, Israeli settlers attacked three Palestinian villages near Ramallah, setting fire to vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on residential buildings.
Eisenkot, leader of the Yashar party, described the attacks as "Jewish terrorism in every sense of the word" and called on the government and security establishment to take tougher action against violent settlers.
"The acts of sabotage carried out by extremist groups setting fire to vehicles and homes undermine regional stability, endanger lives and seriously harm Israel's national security and foreign relations," he
wrote
on X.
Opposition leader Yair Lapid also
condemned
the attacks, calling them "Jewish terrorism" caused by government negligence.
"Jewish terrorism is the product of criminal negligence on the part of the Israeli government," Lapid said. "By remaining silent, government ministers are deliberately encouraging these pogroms."
"When we form a government, we will tackle this terrorism and restore governance, law and order," he added.
In the United States, Democratic Congressman Josh Gottheimer condemned the attacks and called for accountability.
"These incidents warrant a full and thorough investigation," Gottheimer
wrote
on X, adding that vigilante justice had "no place" in society.
Israeli police said they had opened investigations into arson, vandalism and property damage.

items.title: Analysis-Can climate diplomacy build on the collapse of COP31?
items.content:
By Peter Hobson, Simon Jessop, Valerie Volcovici and Sarah McFarlane
ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 23 (Reuters) - The collapse of COP31 talks in Turkey on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight against climate change.
For the small, vulnerable countries most exposed to rising sea levels and the increasingly extreme weather scientists link to rising carbon emissions, annual UN conferences are their chance to draw the world's attention to their plight and seek financial help.

items.title: Workers shot, villagers trapped: Israeli forces and settlers attack Palestinian towns across West Bank
items.content:
Workers shot, villagers trapped: Israeli forces and settlers attack Palestinian towns across West Bank
Israeli forces and settlers carried out raids and attacks across the occupied West Bank on Sunday, injuring and detaining Palestinians, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported. The attacks come amid a sharp escalation in settler violence in the territory.
Overnight into Sunday, Israeli settlers attacked three Palestinian villages,
setting fire
to 12 vehicles and spray-painting racist slogans on residential buildings.
The attacks targeted Kafr Malik, Deir Abu Mash'al and Deir al-Sudan, in the Ramallah and al-Bireh governorate.
Near Hizma, north-east of Jerusalem, Israeli forces fired live ammunition at
Palestinian workers
trying to cross the separation wall into the city, wounding several of them, according to the Jerusalem Governorate.
Around 18 workers were detained, and video footage showed one of them being severely beaten.
The Palestine Red Crescent said it treated two people who were injured after being beaten by Israeli forces and falling from the wall. Israeli forces later closed the entrances to Hizma and forced shops to shut.
In al-Mughayyir, north-east of Ramallah, several Palestinians were injured by flying glass when settlers attacked vehicles on Sunday evening, the head of the village council, Amin Abu Alia, told Wafa.
Abu Alia said settlers, protected by Israeli forces, gathered at the village entrances and
prevented
residents from entering or leaving. He added that Israeli forces detained several Palestinians, and that there was no information so far on their fate or whereabouts.
Many Palestinian residents were also left stranded in the neighbouring village of Abu Falah, unable to return home.
South of Jenin, Israeli forces raided the towns of Anza, Jaba', Arraba and Ya'bad.
Video footage
showed Palestinian man severely beaten by Israeli soldiers inside his house in Ya'bad.
In Azzun Atma, south of Qalqilya, Israeli forces demolished a Palestinian family home of around 120 square metres and a poultry farm, the village council said.
In the northern Jordan Valley, Israeli settlers ploughed around 50 dunams of Palestinian-owned land in the al-Farsiya area.
Palestinian man inspects the burnt-out vehicles following an attack by Israeli settlers, in Kafr Malik near the city of Ramallah in the occupied West Bank, 22 November 2026 (Zain Jaafar/AFP)

Jay Clayton, the US director of national intelligence, said he trusts Donald Trump “completely” after the US president called Vladimir Putin “a friend” during

Clayton made the remarks on Sunday, where he was pressed during media appearances on Trump’s warm characterization of the Russian president – who is viewed as a chief US adversary – following his trilateral summit with Putin and China’s Xi Jinping. posted a photo of himself and Putin
shaking hands with the caption “My Friend.”

Cabinet minister
Murray Watt
says it’s increasingly difficult to bridge the divide between nations on climate policy after a frustrating Cop summit that didn’t reach a final agreement.
It’s obviously a very deeply disappointing outcome that the cover decision was not agreed to by all nations.
I think what this shows is a very challenging international environment at the moment to reach agreement on almost anything and particularly a situation like this where you’ve got fossil fuel producers on the one hand and other countries that are experiencing very serious impacts from climate change.
We’re seeing much greater defence engagement between Australia and Japan, Australia and the Philippines, and the Philippines and Japan.
Even though I think it doesn’t quite come across in its overall score, that US defence relationship in the region is stronger, which is helping Australia.

items.content:
John Kennedy looks to Trump leaders as he asks how China evidently bypassed export controls for Nvidia’s top AI chips
Invoking Greek mythology, US senator John Kennedy has characterized former
Nvidia
chief executive officer
Jensen Huang
’s reported affair with a suspected Chinese spy as “the
most expensive
sex since Helen of Troy”.
The Louisiana Republican’s allusion to the legendary figure whose desirability was such that it caused the mythic Trojan war came during an interview on NBC’s Meet the Press on Sunday. Host Kristen Welker asked Kennedy, known for his colloquialisms, if US national security was
put at risk
by Huang’s affair, given the position his company’s chips have occupied at the forefront of the artificial intelligence boom.

items.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming government
items.content:
Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming government
The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.
Delegations from Eisenkot’s Yashar party and Netanyahu’s Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday.
“The latest round of coalition talks… has concluded. The two sides outlined their positions on a range of substantive issues and discussed them in detail,” the two parties said in a joint statement.
“A follow-up meeting will be held,” they added, without specifying a date or revealing any other details.
A former army chief of staff, Eisenkot has until 6 December to form a government, with the possibility of a 14‑day extension, after October elections failed to give either camp an absolute majority.
His 48-member bloc, which needs 61 lawmakers to reach a majority, remains divided over whether to build a coalition through an alliance with ultra‑Orthodox parties, a rapprochement with Arab parties, or a national unity government with Likud.
Netanyahu is pushing for a national unity government, which could see a rotation of the premiership between the two men.

items.title: Two Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in northern and central Gaza
items.content:
Two Palestinians killed by Israeli fire in northern and central Gaza
Israeli forces killed two Palestinians in separate attacks in the Gaza Strip on Sunday, the Palestinian news agency Wafa reported.
One was shot dead by Israeli gunfire in Jabalia, north of Gaza, on Sunday evening.
Earlier in the evening, an Israeli quadcopter drone struck and killed another Palestinian in eastern Deir al-Balah, in central Gaza.
Israel has killed more than 1,600 Palestinians in Gaza since the ceasefire agreement of October 2025.
At least 74,742 Palestinians have been killed and 176,227 wounded since the war began in October 2023.

items.title: Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
items.content:
Bahrain says Iranian strike wounds two, one critically
Bahrain said on Sunday that two people were wounded in an Iranian strike the previous day on “a civilian industrial site” in the Gulf kingdom, which has faced several attacks this week.
Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) has repeatedly said they targeted US facilities in Bahrain, where Iranian strikes resumed earlier in November.
"In the wake of the criminal Iranian attacks suffered yesterday (Saturday) by the Kingdom of Bahrain… a Bahraini national with a disability was wounded," Bahrain's interior ministry said on X.
"His condition is stable. A Pakistani resident was also wounded and is in critical condition."
Residents had seen smoke rising above Sitra Island, east of Manama, which hosts several industrial facilities, including a refinery operated by the state-owned oil company Bapco, AFP reported.
In a statement carried by Iranian state media on Saturday evening, the IRGC said they had attacked US Patriot air defence systems with missiles and drones at the Al-Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain, in response to the “continued violations of the airspace” of the Islamic Republic.
Bahrain's foreign ministry dismissed the IRGC's account, saying the site hit was purely civilian and industrial, calling the attack a direct danger to civilians and a violation of the kingdom's sovereignty.
Bahrain's neighbour Saudi Arabia on Sunday also condemned Tehran for its attacks on Gulf countries.
The Saudi foreign ministry expressed on X "the strongest condemnation and denunciation... of the criminal Iranian attacks against a civilian industrial facility in the brotherly Kingdom of Bahrain".
As a result of the heinous Iranian attacks on Bahrain yesterday, a Bahraini citizen with disabilities sustained injuries and is in stable condition, while a Pakistani resident was also injured and is in critical condition. Both are receiving treatment in the hospital. #Bahrain #MOI
— وزارة الداخلية - Ministry of Interior (@moi_bahrain)
November 22, 2026

items.title: Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
items.content:
Iran unveils new launcher that can fire two missiles at once
Iran has unveiled a new missile launcher, as senior military commanders touted the Islamic Republic's capabilities in defiant messages to the United States.
"A launcher capable of firing two liquid-propellant missiles simultaneously was unveiled for the first time," Iranian state television reported on Saturday.
State television broadcast footage of Ahmad Vahidi, commander of Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and Majid Mousavi, head of the IRGC's Aerospace Force, touring an underground missile base.
The two commanders were shown riding on top of a vehicle through long tunnels lined with missiles, launchers and other military equipment.
"The damage suffered by our enemy is only the beginning. We shall witness their humiliation," Vahidi said.
"Our capabilities have grown during the last two conflicts, and our high-performance weaponry can intimidate the enemy," said Mousavi.
During the US-Israeli war on Iran, strikes targeted the country's missile capabilities and hit its nuclear sites for a second time, though the extent of the damage remains unclear.
Earlier this month, the IRGC unveiled what it described as new underground "missile cities" housing ballistic and cruise missiles, as well as launchers.

items.title: Libya's eastern government suspects drone attack caused explosion on Russian ship
items.content:
By Ayman Al-Warfali
Nov 22 (Reuters) - A suspected drone attack caused an explosion aboard a Russian ship docked at the Benghazi naval base in eastern Libya, the country's eastern-based government said on Sunday after a preliminary investigation.
No one has claimed responsibility for the suspected attack, and there was no immediate reaction from Russian authorities.
Since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Ukrainian forces have repeatedly used naval drones and missiles to target Russian warships and naval facilities, mainly in the Black Sea.

A drone strike destroyed a house, a witness said, while a Sudanese army source said the drones had been launched from Ethiopia.

items.title: Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
items.content:
Two supertankers hit mines near Hormuz, Iranian navy says
Iran's navy said on Sunday that two supertankers hit naval mines and caught fire after entering a "restricted area" east of the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported.
According to the Fars news agency, the navy said the tankers had switched off their detection and navigation systems and struck the mines north of Ghanam Island.
Both vessels reportedly stopped moving.
Supertankers usually carry two million barrels of oil or more, about twice as much as a standard tanker.
The navy also warned that relying on "smugglers such as CENTCOM", referring to US Central Command, would result in "nothing but heavy losses".
UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) also said on Sunday it had received a report of an incident involving a tanker and military forces in the Gulf of Oman.
It gave no further details, saying only that authorities were aware and an investigation was under way. It was unclear whether the incident involved either of the tankers Iran described.

items.title: From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah
items.content:
From arson to land seizures: Settlers tighten grip on Palestinian villages near Ramallah
Submitted by
Fayha Shalash
on
Sun, 11/22/2026 - 13:25
The attacks come amid a sharp rise in settler violence during the olive harvest, with the UN documenting a record 467 incidents in October
An Israeli settler stands between Israeli forces and Palestinians protesting an alleged arson attack in Idna, west of Hebron, occupied West Bank, 5 June 2026 (Hazem Bader/AFP)
Off
In a series of coordinated attacks across several villages near the city of Ramallah in the central occupied West Bank,
Israeli
settlers torched
Palestinian
vehicles between Saturday evening and Sunday morning.
The settlers also spray-painted racist slogans on the walls of homes in the three villages, calling for the killing of Arabs and for revenge against them.
Rafat Abu Musa, head of the village council of Deir al-Sudan, north of Ramallah, told Middle East Eye that settlers infiltrated the southern part of the village at 11.30pm on Saturday and burned down two vehicles.
The settlers spray-painted slogans in Hebrew on the walls of nearby houses, he said, adding that the same area had been targeted by a similar attack two months ago, during which a vehicle was set on fire.
The settlers, he said, came from a newly built outpost on the summit of Jabal al-Ras, located in the neighbouring village of Umm Safa.
"The fire department was delayed in reaching the scene because they require coordination with the Israeli army; by the time they arrived, the vehicles had already been reduced to ashes," he said.
According to Abu Musa, some five months ago, the settlers seized "an entire mountain" in the southern part of the village, where they established an outpost and constructed roads.
The outpost has deprived residents of access to more than half of the village’s olive trees, as settlers assault the residents and prevent them from approaching their own land, he said.
"This fierce onslaught is being directed by extremist Israeli ministers; these are systematic and recurring attacks," Abu Musa said.
The area where the vehicles were torched is classified as 'Area A'. Under the Oslo Accords, the region is supposed to be under exclusive Palestinian control.
Fake investigations
A few hours after the attack in Abu Musa's village, settlers set fire to seven vehicles in the town of Kafr Malik, east of Ramallah.
More than ten settlers infiltrated the northern part of the town, arriving from an outpost they had established between Kafr Malik and al-Mughayyir; a journey that required them to trek for at least an hour along a rugged mountain path, Jihad Qaq, a resident, told Middle East Eye.
'Jewish terrorism in every sense': Eisenkot blames Smotrich and Ben Gvir for settler attacks
Read More »
He said that the settlers reached Palestinian homes, set the vehicles on fire and wrote racist slogans on the walls of the houses before withdrawing.
"An hour after the attack, the Israeli army stormed the town, forced the civil defence crews who were in the process of extinguishing the fires to leave and drove away the residents."
"They conducted an investigation, but then withdrew without any results," Qaq said.
He said that the village is constantly subjected to harassment by settlers, who, a year and a half ago, burned vehicles in the southern part of the area and killed three young men.
"Settler herders have prevented more than 70 percent of the Palestinian olive harvesters from reaching their land this year, assaulting and beating them," he said.
According to data from the Commission Against the Wall and Settlements, attacks by Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank saw a marked increase this past October, coinciding with the olive harvest season.
Settlers carried out 1,369 attacks during the month, a 112 percent rise compared to September, which saw 647 such incidents.
Relentless attacks
Meanwhile, in the eastern part of the village of Deir Abu Mashal west of Ramallah, classified as 'Area B', settlers burned eight vehicles and wrote racist slogans.
Jamil Musa, head of the village council, said that the settlers arrived from an outpost they had established a few months ago, one of several such outposts they have set up in the vicinity of the village.
Israeli settlers kill Palestinian grandmother in her home in Jericho
Read More »
He said that the attack took place at 2.30am, and the group, consisting of eight to 10 individuals, withdrew from the village after painting racist slogans.
"The Israeli army raided the village and promised to launch an investigation, but nothing has come of it. They also told us that the Israeli police would follow up, but they have yet to arrive," he stated.
Two months ago, settlers set fire to vehicles in the village. In June 2025, they assaulted several families and beat five young men, leaving them with serious injuries.
Residents are unable to access nearly half of the village’s land for the olive harvest due to attacks by settlers, who have been assaulting Palestinians farmers.
The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (Ocha) documented 467 settler attacks that resulted in injuries or property damage during the month of October alone, the highest monthly figure since the organisation began tracking such incidents in 2006.
Over the course of the year, from the beginning of January through 19 October, Ocha recorded 2,159 settler attacks, an average of 7.4 incidents per day, compared to a daily average of five attacks throughout 2025.
According to Ocha, these attacks were particularly concentrated during the olive harvest season.
Between 1 September and 19 October, 272 attacks linked to the harvest were recorded, resulting in the killing of one Palestinian, injuries to 200 others and the destruction of more than 3,200 olive trees.

items.title: Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's Rabigh oil refinery
items.content:
Houthis say they attacked Saudi Arabia's Rabigh oil refinery
Yemen's Houthis said on Sunday they had attacked
Saudi Arabia
's Rabigh oil refinery on the kingdom's Red Sea coast north of Jeddah.
Saudi authorities did not immediately comment.
The Houthis have claimed a string of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure in recent months.
The kingdom's Red Sea coast has become increasingly important to its oil exports, with Riyadh using its East-West pipeline to move crude from the Gulf to western ports, rather than through the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Theresa May’s blast from the past calls Tories back to their unhappy place | Peter Walker
items.content:
Conservatives may instinctively want to push back against closer EU ties, but they have to train their focus elsewhere
Anyone who accidentally switched to BBC One at about 9.45am on Sunday to be greeted by Theresa May
awkwardly espousing
the virtues of Brexit could have been forgiven for thinking they had woken up in around 2018 – and not being especially pleased at the idea.
This is one of the problems now facing May’s party. For all that it is a reflex action for Conservatives to push back against closer ties with the EU, Andy Burnham’s decision to pursue such a course plunges them back into their own unhappy place.

items.content:
مستوطنون إسرائيليون يحرقون ممتلكات فلسطينية في أربع قرى بالضفة الغربية
أضرم مستوطنون إسرائيليون، ليلة السبت إلى الأحد، النار في مركبات وممتلكات فلسطينية في أربع قرى بالضفة الغربية المحتلة، وكتبوا شعارات وعبارات تهديد باللغة العبرية على جدران المنازل، وفق مصادر فلسطينية و أخرى من السلطات الإسرائيلية. وتعتبر هذه الحادثة هي الأحدث في سلسلة من الاعتداءات التي تشهدها المنطقة وسط تصاعد عنف المستوطنين.

items.title: فرنسا: محافظ يطلب إعفائه من مهامه بعد تحقيق قضائي حول تسريب معلومات سرية لحزب مارين لوبان
items.content:
فرنسا: محافظ يطلب إعفائه من مهامه بعد تحقيق قضائي حول تسريب معلومات سرية لحزب مارين لوبان
طلب الأمين العام السابق لوزارة الداخلية الفرنسية، هوغ موتو، إعفائه من مهامه كمحافظ لإقليم سنتر-فال-دو-لوار (وسط فرنسا) بعد أن وجد نفسه في قلب تحقيق قضائي على خلفية شبهات بشأن دوره في تسريب معلومات سرية إلى حزب "التجمع الوطني" اليميني المتطرف. وترتبط هذه المعلومات بتحقيقات قضائية تتعلق بحزب مارين لوبان، التي تضعها استطلاعات الرأي ضمن أبرز المرشحين للانتخابات الرئاسية الفرنسية المقررة عام 2027.

👈 اقرأ المزيد: https://f24.my/CIfp.g

items.title: UK taxpayers held more than £1tn in offshore tax havens, latest HMRC data shows
items.content:
Figures show recent 10% rise in total held in financial centres such as Jersey and Panama, raising fears over cost to public purse
The amount of money UK taxpayers hold in offshore accounts in tax havens has exceeded £1tn for the first time, raising concerns about potential losses to the public purse.
HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) data, obtained by the TaxWatch thinktank through freedom of information requests, shows between 2022 and 2024 the value of balances held offshore in tax havens increased by 10%. These were the latest available figures.

items.title: Netanyahu rival condemns ‘Jewish terrorism’ after settler attacks on Palestinian villages
items.content:
Dozens of militant Israeli settlers raided communities on Saturday night, setting fire to vehicles and several homes
Arson attacks by militant Israeli settlers on Palestinian villages in the occupied West Bank have caused a political row in Israel, drawing condemnation from Gadi Eisenkot, the opposition leader, who described them as “Jewish terrorism”.
Dozens of settlers raided Palestinian communities overnight on Saturday,
setting fire to about a dozen vehicles
and several homes and scrawling racist graffiti. At least four communities were attacked. Israeli police said they had launched an investigation with forensic teams.

items.title: Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
items.content:
Why is Turkey warning of an Israeli military operation in Syria?
Submitted by
Reem Aouir
on
Sun, 11/22/2026 - 13:21
FM Hakan Fidan says Israel is flying weapons to an armed Druze group in southern Syria every week to provoke the Syrian army, and that Ankara has warned Washington
A man hangs a poster of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu beside a Druze flag in Majdal Shams, Israeli-annexed Golan Heights, 17 October 2026 (Jalaa Marey/AFP)
Off
Turkey
's foreign minister has warned that
Israel
could launch a military operation in
Syria
, accusing it of backing a faction within the country's Druze community in an attempt to provoke the Syrian army and create a pretext for intervention.
Hakan Fidan made the remarks in a televised interview with Turkish broadcaster TGRT Haber on Saturday, saying Ankara had raised the possibility with regional allies, as well as US and European officials.
"There is a scenario in which the Israeli army uses this as a pretext to launch an operation against Syria," Fidan said.
The Turkish foreign minister also alleged that Israel was supporting one of three major factions within Syria's Druze community, supplying it with weapons and ammunition by helicopter on a weekly basis.
“In southern Syria, as you know, there are Druze. These Druze are divided into three major tribes within Syria. Two of these are genuinely on the side of the Syrian government and are anti-Israel. But one of them is supported by Israel.”
He claimed the faction was seeking to provoke Syrian government forces, potentially giving Israel justification to intervene militarily.
Omer Ozkizilcik, a non-resident senior fellow at the Atlantic Council, described Ankara’s warning as a precautionary move.
“Turkey's public warning aims at preventing Israel from doing something stupid in southern Syria before Israel actually does it,” he told Middle East Eye.
Fidan’s warning comes amid continued Israeli military activity in southern Syria and unresolved tensions between Damascus and Druze armed groups in the southern province of Sweida.
Sweida, the Druze-majority province in southern Syria, has been run as a de facto area under the spiritual leader Sheikh Hikmat al-Hijri, who has publicly aligned himself with Israel.
Most of its armed factions are grouped under the Sweida National Guard, a coalition of Druze militias backed by Israel and allied with al-Hijri.
Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan says Israel is supplying a Druze faction in southern Syria with weapons and ammunition by helicopter every week, seeking to provoke the Syrian army. Fidan warned that Israel intends to use these provocations as a pretext to launch a military operation and push further into Syrian territory. He said two of Syria’s three major Druze tribal groups support the Syrian government and oppose Israel, while the third is backed by Tel Aviv.
— Middle East Eye (@MiddleEastEye)
November 22, 2026
In July, al-Hijri suggested that Sweida could be integrated into Israel to preserve its autonomy.
Last month, The National reported, citing unnamed sources, that Israeli helicopters had dropped surveillance, radar and other equipment inside Sweida.
Flying over the Yarmouk River basin and villages in Deraa on the way to Sweida, sniper rifles and night-vision systems had also reached the National Guard.
A senior Syrian government official also told The Jerusalem Post in October that an Israeli helicopter had landed in Sweida and delivered significant quantities of weapons and ammunition.
Ozkizilcik also pointed to reports of Israeli helicopters arriving in Sweida and senior Israeli Druze military commanders visiting the province and meeting relatives, describing them as indications that tensions could be building.
"There is something potentially growing, but it's too early to clearly assess," he said.
'Destabilising neighbours'
Last week, the UN's deputy special envoy for Syria, Claudio Cordone, told the Security Council that Damascus had deployed additional forces to Sweida amid reports of continued Israeli support for local armed actors.
He said the province "remains in a tense security and political stalemate".
Supporters of Druze faction raise Israeli flags in Sweida on 7 October anniversary
Read More »
Fidan's remarks came days after he hosted his Syrian counterpart, Asaad al-Shaibani, in Ankara, where he called on Israel to halt its attacks in southern Syria and base its security arrangements on the 1974 Disengagement of Forces Agreement.
"The security of any state cannot be built upon the destabilisation of its neighbours," Fidan said at the joint press conference on Tuesday.
Ozkizilcik described Ankara's warning as a precautionary move intended to deter Israel from launching an operation in southern Syria.
"Turkey is trying to raise awareness and prevent it from happening," he said.
Ankara is a close ally of Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa's government.
In August, Israel struck the Abu al-Duhur airbase, about 70km from the Turkish border, later saying Damascus had been preparing to let Turkey deploy radar and air-defence systems operated by Turkish personnel there.
US envoy Tom Barrack later said the strike had been intended to bait Ankara.
“If Israel launched a major military ground offensive in southern Syria, this would open Pandora’s box for all kinds of military escalation,” Ozkizilcik told MEE.
Why is Syria considering joining the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact?
Read More »
He said such an offensive could turn into a wider confrontation involving Turkey, even if Ankara was reluctant to deploy its own troops directly.
"I do not see a scenario in which Turkey would not be involved in a military escalation against Israel," he said.
He added that Ankara would likely support the Syrian army and coordinate with Arab allies.
“It would be a disaster for Israel militarily, and also politically and diplomatically,” he said.
Ozkizilcik said the risk of Israeli escalation in Syria should also be viewed against the backdrop of Benjamin Netanyahu’s domestic political uncertainty, arguing that the Israeli prime minister had previously used military action to improve his electoral prospects.
“If he cannot go to war again against Iran due to American obstacles, the most likely area for him to launch a new war might be Syria,” he said.
In April, Fidan also stated that Israel was holding back from some actions in Syria because of the war on Iran, but had not abandoned them.
"Later, when the time comes, it may want to act," he said at the time.
'Israel first' vs 'America first'
During the interview, Fidan also shed light on
Gaza
and accused Israel of blocking thousands of container homes that Turkey had prepared for Gaza.
He said Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan had ordered that the units, which Turkey used to house survivors of the 2023 earthquakes, be sent to the enclave.
"Israel is not allowing the containers to enter Gaza on the grounds that they are made of metal," Fidan said.
'Will throw keys back to UN': Trump-appointed Board of Peace adviser says Israel blocking efforts
Read More »
Israel claimed Hamas could use the metal to manufacture weapons, he added.
Fidan also described an ongoing "hidden struggle" in the
United States
between forces that put "Israel first" and those that put "America first".
He said US policy in the Middle East had for decades often served Israeli interests more than American ones, and that Netanyahu's policies had harmed Trump.
"Trump, who boasted of being a man who makes peace, seemed to have become a president who enters wars instead of achieving peace, and who fights on behalf of Israel," Fidan said.
He added that a growing current in the US was rejecting military intervention, and that public hostility towards Israel was rising.
Fidan also defended Turkey's role in the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, signed with
Saudi Arabia
and
Pakistan
in August, which commits each member to treat an attack on one as an attack on all three.
He said Ankara was giving Riyadh the defence support it needed, but accused critics in Turkey of exaggerating the pact.
He dismissed warnings in Turkey that soldiers would die in
Yemen's
desert, saying that unlike a century ago, when Yemen was Ottoman territory, it was now an independent state.
He also noted that Turkey had sent troops to Afghanistan as part of
Nato
without facing similar criticism.
"Why was there no problem when it concerned Nato, while there is a problem when it concerns a regional defence alliance in an Islamic region?" he said.

items.title: Netanyahu, Eisenkot parties end talks without deal on forming Israel govt
items.content:
The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot concluded a new round of talks on Sunday without reaching an agreement on a possible coalition government, which would require concessions from both sides.
Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud met for four hours at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, following a first round of discussions last Sunday.

items.title: Netanyahu and Eisenkot parties resume talks to form Israel govt
items.content:
The parties of caretaker Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his rival Gadi Eisenkot launched a new round of talks on Sunday over whether to form a coalition government, with Netanyahu's party insisting on keeping his main policies.
Delegations from Eisenkot's Yashar party and Netanyahu's Likud began their confab at a hotel in Herzliya, near Tel Aviv, an AFP journalist on the scene said, following a first round of talks last Sunday.

items.title: Israel: Eisenkot and Netanyahu parties meet again for unity government talks
items.content:
Israel: Eisenkot and Netanyahu parties meet again for unity government talks
Representatives from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's Likud party and the party of his main rival, Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar, met on Sunday to discuss forming a unity government, Haaretz is
reporting
.
The meeting follows earlier talks last Sunday after nearly a month of deadlock in the Israeli Knesset since October's election, which saw no party gain an overall majority. Both Netanyahu and Eisenkot have so far failed to negotiate a viable coalition government alongside smaller parties.
Absent from Sunday's meeting were representatives of Naftali Bennett's Together party, which received the third-largest vote share and attended the previous round of talks.

items.title: ستة أيام من الانتظار.. أين البحّار الأردني محمد العتيبي المفقود في مضيق هرمز؟
items.content: تعيش عائلة البحّار الأردني محمد العتيبي حالة من القلق والترقب، عقب فقدانه في مضيق هرمز جرّاء استهداف ناقلة نفط إماراتية كان يعمل على متنها يوم الثلاثاء 17 نوفمبر/تشرين الثاني.
